validated_top_candidate.title: Tip- and Euler-depth-cluster-protected mid-segment flank-shadow de-jittering on d=2.8
layers: labels.tif (catalogue distance d_cat, skeleton endpoints d_end, 3x3 neighbor count cat_nbrs)
evidence/h31_1_euler_clusters.csv (6,309 retained SI=0 Reid et al. 1990 Euler depth-coherent clusters, d_euler <= 300 m)
validated_top_candidate.signature: Remove 100 m lateral digitisation-jitter shadow along interior mapped fault segments (d_cat <= 100 m AND d_end > 300 m AND cat_nbrs >= 2 AND d_euler > 300 m = 2,434 px on d=2.8), while explicitly preserving along-strike tip continuations (d_end <= 300 m: 1,360 px) and shallow Euler N=0 contact depth-cluster corroboration zones (d_euler <= 300 m: 143 px; 1,457 union protected pixels).
validated_top_candidate.why_missing_faults: Hermant et al. (2025, Fig. 2 & Fig. 9B) document up to 400 m lateral offsets between regional USGS Quaternary traces and 1 m LiDAR scarps. Along interior segments (cat_nbrs >= 2, d_end > 300 m) without an independent subsurface contact solution, a d_cat=100 m pixel is lateral digitisation halo on an already-mapped fault (0.0040 credit/FP, 4.8x below OOF break-even). At fault tips (d_end <= 300 m) or where a shallow Euler N=0 depth cluster corroborates a subsurface contact, the pixel marks an unmapped tip propagation or shallow buried splay (0.0092 credit/FP, 2.29x higher credit density).
validated_top_candidate.differs_from_repo: Prior H27-4 blindly pruned all 3,891 d_cat <= 100 m pixels on d=2.8 and was only shipped bundled with the now live-refuted T-v2 gap-closure dots (23ad46a4d7ba). Prior H31-1 fed Euler rasters into a 41-band GBDT and failed screen (-0.00195). H32-1 uses retained SI=0 Euler depth clusters and catalogue tip geometry as a structural protection gate on d=2.8 with zero T-v2 drag.
validated_top_candidate.confounders: Catalogue-internal holdout overweights tip adjacency relative to isolated far-field faults; mitigated by reporting both H32-1 (protected) and solo H27-4 (unprotected) on d=2.8.
validated_top_candidate.cost: Low (~95 s CPU holdout + ~9 s GeoTIFF build); zero external downloads.

ranking_basis: Expected DTI gain multiplied by validation tractability divided by implementation cost. The 4 items in hypotheses[] below are the remaining untried geological hypotheses after validating H32-1.

hypotheses.title: Shallow-over-deep magnetic gradient de-screening (intrusive-pluton margin suppression)
hypotheses.signature: Upward-continuation attenuation ratio R_shallow = |nabla_H(TMI)| / (|nabla_H(TMI_up150)| + eps) paired with shallow basement/magnetic-sediment thickness. Shallow brittle fault contacts (z_0 <= 300 m) decay rapidly under 150 m upward continuation (high R_shallow), whereas deep Cenozoic pluton margins and caldera ring complexes (z_0 >= 1.5-3 km) decay slowly (low R_shallow ~ 1) while still generating strong raw tmi_hg ridges.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Concealed shallow intrabasinal fault contacts beneath thin alluvial cover (mag_sed_thick_km < 0.8 km) lack LiDAR scarps and are omitted from the Quaternary scarp-biased compilation, whereas deep intrusive-body boundaries in ranges produce false-positive far-field magnetic ridges that are not brittle faults.
hypotheses.confounders: Shallow subhorizontal volcanic flow edges can also exhibit high upward-continuation decay; requires cross-checking against topographic contour parallelism.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: TMI_up150 in geodawn_extensions_u8.tif was only appended as an un-ratioed uint8 column in the failed H27-12 +rad/+all detector screen; its horizontal-gradient attenuation ratio against tmi_hg has never been computed or used to de-screen far-field H19-5 ridges.
hypotheses.cost: Low (~25 min implementation + 4-fold spatial-CV holdout; all inputs restored and hash-verified locally).
hypotheses.data_gate: All bands present locally in data/training_features.tif and data/geodawn_extensions_u8.tif (USGS GeoDAWN ScienceBase item 657e1d85d34e23d3533209f7).
hypotheses.validation: Preregister R_shallow far-field ridge swap/filter on d=2.8 before running on unused seeds 190-199.

hypotheses.title: Gravity-gradient bench inflection vs basalt-capped mesa topographic decoupling
hypotheses.signature: Co-aligned local maxima of horizontal gravity gradient (grav_hg) and low-roughness alluvial-fan break-in-slope (det_local_relief, lidar_step_max), contrasted against high-tmi_hg, zero-grav_hg erosional volcanic mesa rims that follow elevation contours.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Pediment-front and older range-front normal faults buried by Holocene fanglomerate aprons lack fresh 1 m LiDAR scarps and are omitted from USGS Qfaults, but juxtapose dense Paleozoic/Mesozoic basement (2,650-2,750 kg/m3) against unconsolidated basin fill (2,000-2,200 kg/m3), creating a persistent grav_hg inflection.
hypotheses.confounders: 2 km regional gravity station spacing limits spatial precision of grav_hg to +-300-500 m; paleochannel incised terraces can mimic low-relief benches.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H28-1 tested magnetic-gravity gradient orientation coherence across all pixels without distinguishing erosional volcanic rims from basement-basin density steps; H27-13 tested oriented LiDAR line integrals without gravity or magnetic decoupling.
hypotheses.cost: Low-medium (~35 min implementation + 4-fold spatial-CV holdout; all bands restored locally).
hypotheses.data_gate: All bands present locally in data/training_features.tif and data/lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif.
hypotheses.validation: Preregister mesa-rim suppression and range-front gravity-bench retention on unused seeds before holdout execution.

hypotheses.title: Quality-screened hydrothermal geothermometer and K/Th-U/Th alteration halos along sub-scarp corridors
layers: data/geodawn_extensions_u8.tif (Th/K, U/K, U/Th airborne radiometric ratios)
hypotheses.signature: Anisotropic fault-strike-aligned hydrothermal alteration corridors coupling quality-screened high-temperature wells/springs (tempc >= 60 C or gt_qtz >= 130 C, de-duplicated to 200 m cells) with potassium-metasomatic depletion of Th/K (low Th/K, elevated U/Th) along sub-threshold geodetector ridges.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Permeable hydrothermal fault conduits in active geothermal districts (e.g., Brady's, Desert Peak, Dixie Valley, Salt Wells) undergo argillic/sericitic alteration that mechanically softens surface rocks and erases brittle scarps, causing omission from Quaternary scarp maps while leaving potassium/uranium radiometric halos and thermal outflows.
hypotheses.confounders: Playa evaporites and felsic tuffs produce non-fault radiometric anomalies; lateral outflow plumes can displace thermal springs 0.5-1.5 km down-gradient from the upflow fault.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H27-12 tested isotropic Euclidean distances to all unscreened wells/springs and raw radiometric bands independently and found near-zero PR-AUC gain (+0.0005 to +0.0007). H26 dilcond-oof-v1 (live 0.1223) used geod_dilaterate x cond_surf alone without hydrothermal points or radiometric K/Th alteration ratios.
hypotheses.cost: Medium (~45 min implementation + fold-safe spatial encoding; all data restored locally).
hypotheses.data_gate: All files present and hash-verified locally in data/gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv and data/geodawn_extensions_u8.tif (GDR #1391 & USGS GeoDAWN).
hypotheses.validation: Preregister quality-screened hydrothermal + Th/K alteration corridor boost on unused seeds before holdout execution.

hypotheses.title: New GDR paleo-geothermal sinter/travertine, 2 m temperature-probe, and Quaternary-volcanics packages
hypotheses.signature: Independent surface hydrothermal-deposit polygons (sinter/tufa/travertine), shallow 2 m thermal-probe anomalies, and Quaternary volcanic unit boundaries marking fault-controlled fluid upflow or dike-fed fissures.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Relict sinter terraces and travertine mounds directly precipitate along fault-hosted fluid conduits even where Holocene sedimentation has buried the surface fault scarp.
hypotheses.confounders: Volcanic flow margins unrelated to tectonic faults, lateral shallow groundwater advection of 2 m temperature plumes, and spatially clustered survey campaigns.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: These three raw zip packages from GDR submission #1391 are not present in data/ (which holds only the 27,092 well/spring rows and 21 volcanic vent points).
hypotheses.cost: High; requires external download outside the github.com/pypi.org sandbox allowlist, SHA-256 verification against sibling pins, and spatial holdout.
hypotheses.data_gate: Official URLs at https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391 are documented and hash-pinned in sibling records (ok:true 2026-09-30), but gdr.openei.org is unreachable from this sandbox environment.
hypotheses.validation: Do not use until official package bytes are retrieved and hash-verified; then preregister each arm on unused seeds.
hypotheses.status: UNTRIED; blocked on external package retrieval.
